question: In January 2022, the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) underlined some green rules for living root bridges of which state to get the UNESCO world heritage site tag?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Zoological Survey of India** (ZSI) highlighted green rules to help the living root bridges of **Meghalaya** get the **UNESCO world heritage site** tag.
 
• These living root bridges are a unique type of bridge found in the northeastern state of India, Meghalaya.
 
• They are made from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees (Ficus elastica) and have been used by the local Khasi and Jaintia tribes for centuries.
 
• The bridges are not only a marvel of bioengineering but also a testament to the harmonious relationship between the local communities and their natural environment.
 
• Efforts to get the UNESCO world heritage site tag aim to preserve these structures and promote sustainable tourism in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The living root bridges are part of the rich cultural heritage of Meghalaya and showcase the ingenious methods used by the indigenous people to adapt to their environment.
 
• UNESCO world heritage site status can help in attracting global attention and resources for the conservation of these unique structures.
 
• Meghalaya is known for its high rainfall and diverse ecosystems, which provide the perfect conditions for the growth of rubber fig trees used in the construction of these bridges.
 
• Conservation efforts will also focus on educating the local communities and tourists about the importance of preserving these natural wonders.
